assumptions: The demonstrated and requested variant is the bilateral, seated, back-supported cable chest press; the explicitly mentioned incline, decline, unsupported-back, and alternating-hand alternatives are excluded.
The concentric phase is from the elbows-flexed start position to handles pressed forward and together, as shown.

The shoulders move primarily through horizontal adduction during the press; the required retracted-scapula instruction is represented as scapular anchoring rather than an unsupported scapular joint-action substitution.
classification_reasons: The instructions, back-supported context, and contact sheet consistently show a seated bilateral cable press with two independently handled cables, elbows extending while the hands converge in front of the torso.
All primary concentric joint actions and required stabilization demands are representable by the supplied vocabulary.
